headline: Green across the board on a red RSI, and the whales are selling into it
paragraphs: Every major on the board sat above its 200-day line except DOGE and ADA, and the crosses mostly agree: SOL, ETH, and BNB are running golden crosses, which is a market where the intermediate trend and the long trend are pointing the same way. That is six of seven majors in a constructive structural posture, with DOGE and ADA the outliers, both still under their 200-day and both a long way from their 12-month highs (-70.1% and -76.9% respectively). Bitcoin itself is up 3.66% on the day, sitting 35.8% below its 12-month high of $124,739.81, which tells you this is a recovery move inside a still-damaged chart, not a fresh breakout.

The momentum readout is where today gets interesting. BTC's RSI-14 is at 71, ETH at 66, BNB at 71.7, all technically overbought by the classic 70 line, and yet BTC and ETH's MACD is below signal, and BNB's is too. That is a real divergence: price and RSI are hot, but the MACD histogram has not confirmed it. SOL is the one asset where RSI (66.9) and MACD (above signal) agree, which makes its trend look the most internally consistent of the group. When RSI says stretched and MACD says not yet confirmed, that is usually a market resting inside a bigger move rather than accelerating cleanly.

Positioning is calm, which is worth noting given the price action. BTC funding on OKX is 0.003% per 8 hours (3.3% annualized), ETH at 1.9% annualized, both mild. XRP stands out at 11% annualized funding with a long/short ratio of 2.32, and DOGE's ratio of 4.08 with 5.8% annualized funding shows a crowd leaning long into a 5.96% day. Liquidations in the last hour were lopsided toward shorts getting squeezed across BTC ($1.34M), ETH ($883K), SOL ($672K), XRP ($983K) and DOGE ($275K), consistent with a move that caught short positioning offside rather than a leveraged long unwind.

The flow picture disagrees with itself and with the price tape. BTC spot ETFs added $101.1M on 02 Sep, extending a five-session net of $121.7M, a real if modest bid. ETH ETFs did the opposite on the same day, $48.2M out, even as the five-session net sits at +$375.9M inflow, a case where the daily print and the trailing window point different ways, so both numbers need their own label rather than a single verdict. Meanwhile whale wallets moved $73.3M net onto exchanges in the last 24 hours, with the biggest single transfers ($162.3M, $116.0M) landing at Coinbase Institutional, the kind of address that can mean custody rebalancing as easily as selling intent. Zoom out to the weekly series and the last three weeks (Aug 13, Aug 20, Aug 27) all show net flow onto exchanges, before flipping to a $368M net move off exchanges in the week ending Sep 03, so today's onto-exchange print is sitting inside a week that, on net, went the other way.

Sentiment reads Greed at 65, inside its own 30-day range of 25 to 74, so the crowd is warm but not pinned to the top of its own recent band. Stablecoin float grew 1.17% over 30 days to $309.2B, a slow build in dry powder rather than a surge. Put together: price up across nearly every major, structure mostly intact above the 200-day, funding cheap outside XRP and DOGE, but RSI stretched without MACD confirmation on three of the biggest names, and whale wallets sending coin toward exchanges on the same day ETFs took in fresh cash. What to watch: whether BTC and ETH's MACD crosses back above signal to confirm the RSI, whether the daily whale flow keeps landing onto exchanges or reverts toward the weekly off-exchange pattern, and whether ETH ETF flows resolve the day-versus-week disagreement in either direction.
